inline:The target's mechanism for centralized resilience (global coordinated mitigation via a control plane) is the very architecture that makes correlated control-plane failure most catastrophic, so it does not establish superior resilience to correlated failure.
The problem asks to argue whether a decentralized network is more/less resilient to correlated failure than one large, strictly-more-redundant service. The target asserts centralized resilience via a global control plane that can detect and isolate failing versions instantly. But its own countercondition concedes the central control plane can become a SPOF. If the shared control-plane logic or shared dependent library is hit by a correlated trigger, all redundant heterogeneous stacks fall under one coordination authority simultaneously. The target provides no evidence distinguishing truly independent mitigation from apparent independence until the shared control plane fails; thus it assumes away the correlated-failure class the problem specifically demands evidence for.
